a.d: Used in newspaper articles, reports, diaries, and novels where the writer records facts objectively without addressing a specific spoken listener.
ex: 정부가 오늘 새로운 경제 정책을 **발표했다**. — The government announced a new economic policy today.

b.d: Used in daily spoken and polite written communication directly directed at an addressee.
ex: 정부가 오늘 새로운 정책을 **발표했어요**. — The government announced a new policy today.

im-c50-01.tip: Use the narrative form (-(느)ㄴ다 for verbs, -다 for adjectives) when writing essays, exam answers, and journals. Avoid using it in spoken conversation with listeners.

im-c50-01.q: Fix the unnatural diary sentence that inappropriately uses conversational honorifics instead of the written narrative form.
im-c50-01.wrong: 오늘 하루 종일 비가 내려서 기분이 조금 우울해요.
answers: 오늘 하루 종일 비가 내려서 기분이 조금 우울했다.
오늘 하루 종일 비가 내려서 기분이 조금 우울했다
오늘 하루 종일 비가 내려서 기분이 조금 우울하다.
오늘 하루 종일 비가 내려서 기분이 조금 우울하다
im-c50-01.hint: In personal journals and reflective writing, use the past narrative ending -았/었다: 우울했다.
im-c50-01.why: Diaries and reflective essays are written in the objective narrative form rather than spoken 해요체.

im-c50-01.hint: While studying for the exam at the library, I ran into a friend.

im-c50-01.q: Write a narrative essay sentence describing the seasonal change to autumn, using 가을이 되자 날씨가 and 선선해진다.
im-c50-01.why: Writing present narrative form with -ㄴ다 for descriptive prose.

steps.en: As autumn arrives, the weather becomes cool morning and evening.
As autumn blows with brisk winds, air cools morning and evening and the weather becomes cool.

ko: 현대 사회에서는 정보 통신 기술의 눈부신 발전으로 사람들의 일상생활에 많은 변화가 나타난다.
이제 사람들은 시공간의 제약 없이 언제 어디서나 전 세계 사람들과 실시간으로 소통한다.
이러한 기술 혁신은 편리함을 가져오는 동시에 새로운 사회적 과제를 낳기도 한다.
en: In modern society, rapid advancements in information and communications technology bring many changes to people's daily lives.
People now communicate in real time with anyone worldwide without constraints of time and space.
Such technological innovations bring convenience while simultaneously generating new societal challenges.

im-c50-01.q: What is the stylistic feature of this passage?
options: An objective written narrative style (서술체) addressed to a general reading audience
A casual spoken chat between high school friends
A formal military command
im-c50-01.why: The text uses -(느)ㄴ다 endings (나타난다, 소통한다, 낳기도 한다) characteristic of written narrative style.

im-c50-01.q: What balanced perspective does the author express regarding technological innovation?
options: It provides convenience while simultaneously bringing new social challenges
It brings only complete disaster with zero benefits
It completely stopped people from communicating
im-c50-01.why: The text concludes '편리함을 가져오는 동시에 새로운 사회적 과제를 낳기도 한다'.

items: I can conjugate verbs and adjectives into written narrative forms (-(느)ㄴ다 · -다).
I can write objective essays, reports, and journal entries in appropriate literary registers.

a.d: Created by dropping '요' from the polite 해요체 form, used strictly with same-age friends or younger family members.
ex: 지금 어디 가? 나랑 같이 점심 **먹자**. — Where are you going now? Let's eat lunch together with me.

b.d: Used with colleagues, elders, teachers, or acquaintances to maintain polite friendliness.
ex: 지금 어디 가세요? 저랑 같이 점심 **먹어요**. — Where are you going now? Please eat lunch together with me.

im-c50-02.tip: Dropping -요 produces casual talk: 가요 -> 가, 먹어요 -> 먹어. Only use with agreed peers and close friends.

im-c50-02.q: Fix the disrespectful sentence mistakenly addressing a university teacher in casual speech.
im-c50-02.hint: Respectful communication with teachers requires polite honorifics: 언제예요?
im-c50-02.why: Casual 반말 forms without '요' are inappropriate when addressing superiors, teachers, or unfamiliar adults.

im-c50-02.say: 오늘 방과 후에 시간 있으면 우리 집에 놀러 와
answers: 오늘 방과 후에 시간 있으면 우리 집에 놀러 와
오늘 방과 후에 시간 있으면 우리 집에 놀러 와.
im-c50-02.hint: If you have time after school today, come hang out at my place.

im-c50-02.q: Write a friendly weekend suggestion to a close classmate, using 주말에 별일 없으면 and 같이 영화 보러 가자.
im-c50-02.sample: 주말에 별일 없으면 같이 영화 보러 가자.
im-c50-02.why: Proposing an outing with a friend in casual speech using -자: 영화 보러 가자.

steps.en: If you have time this weekend, let's go together to the cinema to watch a movie.
If you have no particular plans this weekend, let's head to the local theater and watch a movie together.

ko: 오늘 수업 끝나고 민우랑 오랜만에 떡볶이를 먹으러 골목 분식점에 갔어.
둘이서 학창 시절 추억을 이야기하며 배가 터지도록 웃고 떠들었지.
다음 주말에도 시간 맞춰서 다 같이 한강 공원에 자전거 타러 가기로 약속했어.
en: After class today, I went to an alley snack shop with Minwoo to eat tteokbokki after a long time.
The two of us talked about school memories and chatted and laughed till our bellies burst.
We promised to sync schedules next weekend and all go ride bikes together at Han River Park.

im-c50-02.q: Where did the author and their friend go together after class?
options: An alley snack shop to eat tteokbokki (골목 분식점)
An airport to catch a flight to Paris
A formal five-star hotel ballroom
im-c50-02.why: The text states '민우랑 오랜만에 떡볶이를 먹으러 골목 분식점에 갔어'.

im-c50-02.q: What plan did the two friends make for the upcoming weekend?
options: Riding bicycles together at Han River Park (자전거 타러 가기로)
Taking an official university entrance test
Staying awake 48 hours without food
im-c50-02.why: The text says '다 같이 한강 공원에 자전거 타러 가기로 약속했어'.

items: I can drop '요' from polite forms to converse comfortably with close Korean friends.
I can form casual questions, statements, and proposals (-자) accurately.

im-c50-03.h: 서술체 (Written Plain Form) vs 반말체 (Conversational Casual Form)

a.d: Used in text for unspecified readers without conversational interactivity: '비가 내렸다', '학생들이 책을 읽는다'.
ex: 오늘은 하루 종일 맑은 가을 날씨가 **이어졌다**. — Clear autumn weather continued all day today.

b.d: Used in direct spoken exchanges between close conversational partners: '비가 왔어', '책 읽어?'.
ex: 오늘 하루 종일 날씨가 진짜 **좋았어**. — The weather was really nice all day today.

im-c50-03.tip: Never confuse written narrative endings (-(느)ㄴ다) with casual spoken dialogue. Saying '나 밥 먹는다' in dialogue sounds like thinking aloud.

im-c50-03.q: Fix the unnatural message asking a friend where they are using a written narrative suffix instead of casual dialogue.
im-c50-03.hint: In casual text messages to friends, ask with -아/어 or -니: 어디 가?
im-c50-03.why: The written narrative ending -ㄴ다 is inappropriate for personal interrogative speech directed at friends.

im-c50-03.say: 책이나 신문 기사를 쓸 때는 서술체로 문장을 맺는다
answers: 책이나 신문 기사를 쓸 때는 서술체로 문장을 맺는다
책이나 신문 기사를 쓸 때는 서술체로 문장을 맺는다.
im-c50-03.hint: When writing books or newspaper articles, sentences are concluded in narrative form.
im-c50-03.why: Describing written prose principles: 문장을 맺는다.

im-c50-03.q: Write a sentence stating that reports and articles use objective narrative style, using 신문 기사나 보고서에서는 and 객관적인 서술체를 사용한다.
im-c50-03.sample: 신문 기사나 보고서에서는 객관적인 서술체를 사용한다.
im-c50-03.why: Stating standard literary usage with narrative ending -ㄴ다.

steps.en: Reports and newspaper articles are written in objective narrative style.

tokens: 공식 보고서나 신문 기사 등 독자가 정해지지 않은 글은
steps.en: Writings with unspecified readers like official reports or news articles are always written in objective narrative style.

ko: 서술체와 반말체는 어미 형태가 일부 비슷해 보이지만 쓰이는 상황과 대상이 완전히 다릅니다.
서술체는 독자를 특정하지 않는 신문, 보고서, 논문, 일기 등 글에서 객관적인 사실을 기록할 때 사용합니다.
반면에 반말체는 친한 친구나 손아랫사람과의 실제 대화에서 친밀감을 표현할 때 씁니다.
en: Although narrative written forms and casual informal forms may look partially similar in endings, the contexts and targets they are used in are completely different.
The narrative form is used in written texts such as newspapers, reports, theses, and diaries with unspecified readers to record objective facts.
In contrast, casual informal speech is used in actual conversation with close friends or younger peers to express intimacy.

im-c50-03.q: What is the primary context for using the narrative written form (서술체)?
options: Recording objective facts in essays, news articles, and reports for unspecified readers
Chatting informally with cousins at dinner
Singing karaoke songs aloud
im-c50-03.why: The text states '신문, 보고서, 논문, 일기 등 글에서 객관적인 사실을 기록할 때 사용합니다'.

im-c50-03.q: What purpose does casual informal talk (반말체) serve according to the passage?
options: Expressing intimacy in actual dialogues with close friends or younger peers
Delivering formal diplomatic summits
Publishing academic journal articles
im-c50-03.why: The passage confirms '친한 친구나 손아랫사람과의 실제 대화에서 친밀감을 표현할 때 씁니다'.

items: I can tell apart written narrative forms from spoken casual talk without mixing their roles.
I can match appropriate sentence endings to reading audiences and conversational listeners.

a.d: Used in presentations, official announcements, interviews, and formal workplace interactions.
ex: 지금부터 상반기 프로젝트 최종 결과 보고를 **시작하겠습니다**. — We will now begin the first half project final results report.

b.d: Used during private breaks, casual chats, and friendly social interaction outside strict proceedings.
ex: 회의 끝나고 같이 커피 한잔하러 **갈까요**? — Shall we go drink a cup of coffee together after the meeting?

im-c50-04.tip: Switch naturally: use formal -(스)ㅂ니다 during podium presentations; switch to friendly -아요/어요 during lunchtime coffee.

im-c50-04.q: Fix the impolite question addressed to a team leader during an official company meeting.
im-c50-04.hint: Address superiors respectfully with honorific verb forms: 외근 나가세요? or 외근 가십니까?
im-c50-04.why: Workplace interactions with superiors require proper honorific agreement and polite verb endings.

im-c50-04.sample: 회의 발표를 마친 뒤에는 공손한 격식체로 감사를 전해야 합니다.

base.en: You must change your tone of speech.

steps.en: You must naturally change your tone of speech matching your partner.

tokens: 상대방의 나이와 지위 및 대화 장소에 따라
steps.en: Depending on your partner's age, rank, and the conversation setting, you must politely change your tone of speech appropriately.

ko: 한국어에서는 누구와 대화하느냐에 따라 말투를 자유자재로 전환할 수 있어야 원만한 인간관계를 유지할 수 있습니다.
직장이나 공식 석상에서는 공손한 격식체를 쓰고, 동료와 사적으로 친해졌을 때도 상호 합의 하에 말을 놓아야 합니다.
글을 쓸 때도 독자의 성격과 문서의 형식에 맞추어 서술체와 경어체를 정확히 구분하여 사용하는 태도가 필요합니다.
en: In Korean, being able to freely switch speech styles depending on who you talk with is essential for maintaining smooth human relationships.
In the workplace or formal venues, use polite formal styles, and even when becoming close with colleagues privately, drop honorifics only with mutual consent.
When writing as well, an attitude of accurately distinguishing between narrative and polite styles according to audience and document format is required.

im-c50-04.q: What core communication skill does the author emphasize for smooth social relationships?
options: Freely and appropriately switching speech styles according to partner and situation
Using casual informal talk with everyone right away
Avoiding all spoken conversation permanently
im-c50-04.why: The text states '누구와 대화하느냐에 따라 말투를 자유자재로 전환할 수 있어야 원만한 인간관계를 유지할 수 있습니다'.

im-c50-04.q: What rule of etiquette is advised when shifting to casual speech with friendly colleagues?
options: Dropping honorifics only under mutual consent (상호 합의 하에)
Dropping honorifics unilaterally without asking
Calling everyone by informal nicknames during formal meetings
im-c50-04.why: The text notes '동료와 사적으로 친해졌을 때도 상호 합의 하에 말을 놓아야 합니다'.

items: I can flexibly transition between formal, polite, and casual registers depending on context.
I can communicate respectfully with colleagues and superiors in workplace settings.
